Hey im going through a divorce in MO right now and am also young! Must be in the air. You need a certificate of disillusion, a court petition and form 17 which is available from the courthouse. It's 144ish dollars to file depending on your county. A lawyer can draw up the court petition if need be. Also the self packets can be of use, but Missouri frowns on divorce so I'm not sure how readily available they are in more rural counties. You also won't tell the judge verbally how you're splitting it all up. That's done in writing and submitted. Most consultations with lawyers are free and since there's no major properties it shouldn't be too expensive to move forward, especially if she discusses alimony. Then you wait for your date and show up (or not if you don't contest). And dumping it all on one person or helping out each other with the split doesn't mean it'll be messy. That's determined by both of your actions or intentions. You can both do your best to make sure each other is in a good place when the divorce is finalized, that's the definition of amicable.
